title: Intermittent SSO proxy misroute causes missing audit events and temporary RBAC elevation for private clusters
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Several Private customers reported missing audit events and unexpected permission bypasses during high volume SSO logins. Root cause appears to be a race in the SSO proxy's backend selection logic: when the proxy retries a failed assertion validation against the control plane, it can forward the request to a stale control-plane replica with a missing tenant-mapping cache entry. That path returns a synthetic 2xx for the auth check but omits the tenant header used by downstream RBAC and audit pipelines, resulting in (a) temporary elevation where default RBAC fallback allowed broader access, and (b) audit events not being emitted or tagged to the correct tenant. This only happens intermittently under high authentication concurrency and when control-plane replicas are lagging during config propagation.
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy a Private control plane with 3 replicas and enable SSO via SAML for tenant 'acme-corp'.
Seed a tenant-binding update and stall propagation to replica-2 (simulate network delay / CPU pressure).
Simulate concurrent SSO logins (100+ in a short window) through the SSO proxy that load-balance to replicas.
Observe in the proxy logs: some retries go to the lagging replica and show auth success but missing X-Tenant header downstream.
Check RBAC logs: requests where X-Tenant missing hit fallback policy and are allowed, and audit events are either dropped or lack tenant attribution.
impact_observed: 2 enterprise customers reported 5-20 minutes of incomplete audit trails during a peak onboarding window
One customer observed transient read-access to some tenant-scoped monitoring routes (no data exfiltration confirmed).
SLOs for audit event delivery were breached for affected tenants for the 15-minute window.
investigation_notes: 03/10 09:10 - On-call triaged after PagerDuty alerts from both customer support and the audit ingestion pipeline.
03/10 10:05 - Reproduced locally by throttling control-plane replica propagation; confirmed X-Tenant header missing on retried validation path.

03/11 14:20 - Packet captures and proxy request traces show that the proxy treats certain 'soft' validation failures as retryable, but the retry flow does not rehydrate tenant cache when talking to a different replica.
03/12 08:33 - Security reviewed and agreed to emergency mitigation: change proxy to treat validation retries as short-circuit fails (deny) until cache rehydration is confirmed.
03/13 02:12 - Hotfix PR created to alter retry semantics and add defensive header propagation checks. Unit tests added for header-preservation across retries.
linked_prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2897 - sso-proxy: deny-on-retry behavior and header-preserve guards
https://github.com/redwood-inference/priv-control-plane/pull/1321 - add tenant-cache consistency check and metrics
https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/764 - surface SSO proxy retry metric in Console dashboard
proposed_fix_and_tradeoffs: 1) Immediate mitigation (deployed canary 2026-03-13): change retryable validation to fail-open? No — security risk. We changed to fail-closed for retries meaning proxy returns auth failure rather than silently succeed without tenant header. Tradeoff: small increase in login failures for corner cases, but prevents audit loss and elevation.

2) Medium-term: make tenant cache strongly consistent during config propagation using streaming updates between replicas. Tradeoff: higher coupling and increased control-plane RPCs; work required across control plane and operator docs (estimate 3 sprints).

3) Long-term: add a compact signed tenant assertion in the SAML flow so downstream services can verify tenant identity even if proxy header missing. Tradeoff: protocol change with customer migration effort.
qa_and_rollout_plan: Canary rollout to 3 Private clusters with heavy SSO test traffic (03/13–03/14). Monitor for new 401 spike and audit throughput.
If >0.5% increase in customer-visible login failures over 30m: rollback and revert change; instead apply mitigations to control-plane propagation.
Full rollout planned 03/16 after 48h of canary stability and customer confirmation. Notify affected customers and CS before wide rollout.
current_status_update: 03/13 11:00 - Hotfix deployed to canary clusters. Observed expected small uptick in rejected sessions (~0.2% of auth attempts) and audit delivery restored to normal for canary tenants.
03/14 09:30 - Additional telemetry dashboards added to Console showing retry destinations and header-preservation rates; alerted PM and CSEs.
Pending: coordinate postmortem and track long-term control-plane fix in Private roadmap (linked as PM initiative).
resolution_summary: Hotfix modified SSO proxy retry semantics to fail-closed for validation retries and added header-preservation assertions. Canary shows restored audit delivery and no confirmed privilege escalations after the fix. Medium- and long-term fixes scoped for next quarters to remove the root cause (replica propagation and protocol hardening).
next_steps: Complete formal postmortem and distribute to affected customers by 2026-03-18.
PM to add a ticket for control-plane streaming propagation (PM-4728) and prioritize in Q2 roadmap.
Add e2e test harness to simulate replica lag in CI to prevent regression. (estimate 5 points)
Customer success to coordinate remediation verification with impacted customers and close support cases.
